title: Sequence-histogram-driven KV retention & model-version affinity publish workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an automated publish workflow that generates KV retention recommendations from per-model sequence-length histograms, combines them with model-version affinity scores, and produces safe, reviewable publish artifacts (pin proposals + canary config) for the runtime catalog. This ticket covers the orchestration layer: histogram ingestion, affinity scoring, retention-window suggestions, draft publish artifact generation, and a canary/rollback policy enforced by the Console rollout API.

Background: We have many models with long-tail sequence distributions. Retaining KV for a fixed sequence length per model leads to increased memory and higher p95 latency spikes for tail requests. Previously we published static KV profiles; this work proposes reducing tail risk by combining sequence histograms with historical latency/cost traces to compute a suggested retention curve and an affinity weight to pin specific runtime builds/quantized variants. The output is a publishable artifact that the Console can use for controlled rollouts (canary group, thresholds, fallback variant).

Key concepts: 
- Sequence histogram: compact representation of per-model sequence length distribution (buckets: 0-128,129-512,513-2048,2049-8192,8193+).
- Retention curve: per-bucket recommended KV retention percent (e.g., keep 100% for bucket<=512, 75% for 513-2048, 25% for tail) with TTLs for expiry.
- Affinity score: numeric score expressing model-version compatibility with a runtime variant (e.g., fp16-qat-v2 vs int8q-v1); used to prefer variants when publishing pins.
- Publish artifact: JSON document with model, version, retention_curve, affinity_scores, canary_config, suggested rollout plan and rollback triggers.

Success metrics: 
- Generated retention artifacts reduce estimated memory footprint for top 20 catalog models by >=18% on simulated workload cost model.
- Canary rollouts detect regressions within 15 minutes of start using p95 latency and generation-error rate thresholds.
- Manual review + automated checks must be possible; no automatic pin activation without explicit approval for production models currently in active contracts.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Ingestion pipeline: sequence histograms can be posted to the onboarding API (endpoint documented) and persisted to the profile-store.
2) Affinity scoring: compute and store affinity scores for at least three runtime variants per model-version.
3) Retention generation: algorithm produces a retention_curve and TTLs for all histogram buckets; unit tests covering edge distributions (spiky tail, heavy middle) exist.
4) Publish artifact: a well-formed JSON artifact is produced and uploaded to the publish queue; artifact schema documented in Confluence.
5) Canary config: produce a canary_config with thresholds (p95 latency delta, error rate increase, cost-per-token delta) and rollback actions wired to Console rollout API.
6) End-to-end test: a simulated canary run demonstrates detection and rollback on an injected 12% p95 latency regression.
7) Docs: Confluence page with algorithm description, schema, and rollout playbook updated.

Implementation notes and trade-offs: 
- Deterministic retention curves vs percentile-driven: we prefer percentile-driven retention suggestions (e.g., keep cache for 99th percentile of fast-path sequences) to minimize p95 regressions, but that increases memory. The curve generator exposes a tunable knob (aggressiveness) with safety defaults.
- Affinity scoring uses a lightweight benchmark (100 sample prompts from golden-trace) to estimate delta-latency and delta-quality; heavier benchmarks are expensive but more accurate. For the initial iteration we use latency+KEmetrics (token-level logloss proxy) with configurable weighting.
- We will not auto-promote pins for models that have active reserved capacity contracts; those require manual approval by Platform Ops.

Work breakdown: 
- Histogram ingestion API + persistence (Aisha)
- Curve generator + unit tests (Marco)
- Affinity scorer job + cache (Rina)
- Publish artifact builder + schema (Marco + Aisha)
- Canary config + Console integration (Samir)
- E2E simulation harness and injected-regression tests (Rina + QA)
- Docs and playbook (Aisha)
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha: Spike complete. Implemented prototype histogram schema and small tool to compress sequence traces into 5 buckets. Uploaded sample histograms for gpt-open-7b and gpt-open-13b to /drive/shared/kv-histogram-examples.

2026-02-23 - Marco: Drafted retention curve generator. Default aggressiveness=0.7 gives ~22% mem reduction on dev traces but increases simulated p95 by 4%. We should test lower aggressiveness for enterprise models.

2026-02-26 - Rina: Affinity scorer v0 ready. Uses 100-sample golden trace, measures p95 delta and token-logloss proxy. Results persisted under affinity-cache/v0/2026-02-26. Added REST endpoint to fetch scores.

2026-03-02 - Samir: Console team reviewed canary schema. Requested explicit fields for 'metric_source' and 'alert_channel'. Also asked to add a max-canary-duration default of 30m and staging-only auto-promote disabled.

2026-03-05 - Code review: PR #1482 opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1482) with curve-generator and unit tests. Feedback: make aggressiveness parameter pluggable via job config, add more comments about percentile-to-ttl mapping.

2026-03-09 - QA: E2E harness ran simulated canary with injected 12% p95 regression; rollback triggered after 11 minutes based on p95 delta threshold=+10%. Test artifact: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/canary-sim-ENG-50711
2026-03-11 - Product (Elena): Need clarifying language in Confluence about manual approval gating for Dedicated customers and where to see the suggested memory impact estimate in Console.

2026-03-12 - Marco: Updated publish artifact format to include 'estimated_memory_delta' and 'expected_cost_delta' fields. Uploaded new schema to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/SeqHistogram+Publish+Schema
notes: Follow-on work: wire in model-contract metadata to prevent auto-promotion for committed customers.
Consider adding adaptive re-computation cadence for histograms: weekly for high-traffic models, monthly for low-traffic.
